papers.title: Exploring the association between gastroesophageal reflux disease and hyperlipidemia through bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Observational research has found a relationship between gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and hyperlipidemia (HLP). This study explored the relationship between GERD and HLP using bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization (MR) methods. We first conducted bioinformatics analyses to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from disease datasets and then performed a two-sample MR analysis with aggregated genome-wide association study (GWAS) data to investigate the relationship. 11 DEGs were shared between GERD and HLP. According to the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) en
papers.summary: This study combined bioinformatics differential expression analysis with two-sample Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is causally linked to hyperlipidemia (HLP). The authors identified 11 shared differentially expressed genes between the two conditions and used GWAS summary data to assess a potential causal relationship. The work suggests a genetic and molecular overlap between GERD and HLP, though the abstract is truncated before reporting the MR causal estimate.

papers.title: HisTrader identifies nucleosome-free regions within ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications.
papers.abstract: Enhancers and promoters regulate cell identity through the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA motifs within accessible chromatin. These regulatory regions are often identified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based assays targeting histone modifications, such as ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq), HiChIP, and proximity-ligation-assisted ChIP-seq (PLAC-seq). However, the large size of the enriched regions, or peaks, can make it difficult to pinpoint the precise DNA sequence where TFs act or where trait- or disease-associated variants exert their effects. We present HisTrad
papers.summary: HisTrader is a computational tool that identifies nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) from ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications, such as ChIP-seq, HiChIP, and PLAC-seq. By pinpointing these accessible regions within broad histone modification peaks, the method helps localize precise transcription factor binding sites and trait- or disease-associated variants. This improves the resolution of regulatory element mapping from widely used epigenomic assays.

papers.title: Using Brain Organoids to Explore Human Neurobiology.
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in neuroscience is understanding how the human brain develops into a highly organized and functionally integrated organ, because many developmental processes cannot be investigated directly in humans and are not fully recapitulated in animal models. Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells have emerged as powerful three-dimensional (3D) experimental models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, including regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. Recent advances in long-term organoid culture, organ
papers.summary: This review discusses how brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells serve as 3D models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, such as regional patterning and neural circuit assembly. It highlights recent advances in long-term culture that make these models increasingly useful for studying human neurobiology where animal models fall short.

papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: The authors developed a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention to predict gene expression from epigenetic modifications in fungi. The model enables knowledge transfer across fungal species with different phylogenetic distances, helping to infer expression patterns in less-characterized organisms. This work highlights the potential of deep learning to bridge gaps in epigenetic understanding across non-model species.

papers.title: Beyond the drug-centric view: Advancing AI virtual cell platforms for environmental perturbation modelling.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality, with their biological effects shaped by factors such as dose, exposure duration, life-stage timing, and cumulative or sequential exposure patterns. With rapid advances in AI based virtual cell (VC) technologies, current frameworks emphasize genet-ic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental perturbations insufficiently modelled. This imbal-ance is due to fundamental structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and representa-tional design, as well as lacking standardized
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI virtual cell platforms are heavily biased toward genetic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental exposures—which contribute substantially to global disease burden—poorly represented. The authors attribute this gap to structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and model representation design, and call for standardized frameworks to extend virtual cell modelling to environmental perturbations.

papers.title: CoSAG-nf: A Scalable Nextflow Pipeline for Co-assembly, Optimization, and Interactive Visualization of High-Throughput Single-Cell Genomes.
papers.abstract: Single-cell amplified genomes (SAGs) are crucial for resolving intra-population microbial heterogeneity and accurately understanding the metabolic potential of microbial dark matter populations. However, SAGs generated through multiple displacement amplification (MDA) of genomic DNA from single cells with single-copy chromosomes are highly fragmented and prone to contamination, severely hindering high-quality genome reconstruction and functional analysis, which greatly limits their scientific utility. Co-assembly of related SAGs can substantially improve genome quality, but to our knowledge no
papers.summary: CoSAG-nf is a Nextflow pipeline that co-assembles related single-cell amplified genomes (SAGs) to overcome the fragmentation and contamination typical of MDA-based single-cell sequencing. It provides scalable co-assembly, optimization, and interactive visualization, enabling better reconstruction of high-quality genomes from microbial dark matter populations.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers for central nervous system (CNS) tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histological classification to an integrated molecular framework. It focuses on key genomic and epigenomic markers, particularly DNA methylation profiling, and their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications across major CNS tumor categories.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based epigenetic screening identifies DNA hypermethylation signatures as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Promoter DNA hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing in cancer, yet the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and its prognostic relevance remain poorly characterized. Here, we systematically identified and validated novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance in OSCC using a genome-wide discovery and multi-platform validation strategy. Candidate genes were first identified by pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing across OSCC cell lines, then validated by quantitative RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite se
papers.summary: This study systematically identified DNA hypermethylation events in oral squamous cell carcinoma by combining demethylation drug treatment with RNA sequencing across cell lines, then validating candidates with multiple methylation and expression assays. The identified hypermethylation signatures were linked to patient prognosis, suggesting they could serve as biomarkers for OSCC.

papers.title: Protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes using a hybrid method.
papers.abstract: Borrelia has a linear chromosome and linear plasmids capped by hairpin telomeres that short-read sequencing cannot resolve. Here, we present a protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes. We describe steps for spanning B. burgdorferi culture, DNA extraction, and sequencing through hybrid genome assembly to generate complete Borrelia genomes. The pipeline integrates Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads to assemble hairpin telomeres, resolve paralogous linear and circular plasmids, and annotate and validate the assembled complete Borrelia genome. For complete de
papers.summary: This protocol describes a hybrid sequencing and assembly pipeline that combines Oxford Nanopore long reads with Illumina short reads to produce complete, telomere-to-telomere Borrelia genomes. It addresses the specific challenge of resolving hairpin-capped linear chromosomes and plasmids that short-read sequencing alone cannot assemble. The workflow covers culture, DNA extraction, sequencing, assembly, plasmid resolution, and annotation/validation steps.

papers.title: MACS3: A Peak-calling Platform for Bulk and Single-cell Regulatory Genomics.
papers.abstract: Since the original publication of Model-based Analysis for ChIP-Seq (MACS), the software has been widely used to identify enriched genomic regions in ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, DNase-seq, and related regulatory genomics assays. Over the years, MACS has evolved substantially, with MACS version 3 (MACS3) now serving as the actively maintained implementation. MACS3 preserves the core MACS framework for fragment pileup, dynamic local background noise, statistical enrichment testing, and peak refinement, while adding functionality needed for contemporary bulk and single-cell workflows. It support
papers.summary: MACS3 is the actively maintained successor to the widely used MACS peak-calling software, preserving its core statistical framework for detecting enriched genomic regions while adding support for modern bulk and single-cell regulatory genomics assays. It extends applicability across ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, and DNase-seq workflows.

papers.title: Biological Parts in Yeast Synthetic Biology: From Regulatory Elements to Predictive Design Platforms.
papers.abstract: Yeasts, particularly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, are important eukaryotic chassis for synthetic biology because of their tractable genetics, versatile toolkits, and broad utility in metabolic engineering and functional genomics. Progress in this field has been driven by biological parts that enable programmable control of gene expression and cellular behavior. Early efforts focused mainly on promoters, terminators, and other regulatory elements for tuning individual genes. However, as engineering expanded to multigene pathways, genetic circuits, and dynamic regulatory systems, the limits of part
papers.summary: This review surveys the biological parts used in yeast synthetic biology, tracing the field's evolution from simple regulatory elements like promoters and terminators to more complex systems for controlling multigene pathways and genetic circuits. It highlights how these parts enable programmable control of gene expression and discusses emerging predictive design platforms for engineering yeast.

papers.title: A comprehensive map of the bovine mobilome and their epigenetic regulation of mastitis.
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons are major components of mammalian genomes, yet their genome-wide annotation and epigenetic regulation in cattle remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a comprehensive annotation and integrative epigenomic analysis of major retrotransposon classes in the bovine genome, with emphasis on DNA methylation patterns and their potential roles in subclinical mastitis. Using a multi-step de novo pipeline, we identified and classified long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs), short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs), and endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in the bovine refe
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive genome-wide annotation of retrotransposons (LINEs, SINEs, and ERVs) in the bovine genome using a de novo pipeline, and integrates this with DNA methylation data to explore their epigenetic regulation in the context of subclinical mastitis. The work highlights how retrotransposon methylation patterns may contribute to mastitis susceptibility in cattle.

papers.title: Longitudinal characterization of mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections in a military cohort reveals compartmentalized viral populations.
papers.abstract: Mixed-genotype severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections are a concern due to the potential generation of novel recombinants that give rise to new variants. To better understand intra-host viral dynamics, we analyzed specimens from 24 participants from the U.S. Military Health System's Epidemiology, Immunology, and Clinical Characteristics of Emerging Infectious Diseases with Pandemic Potential COVID-19 cohort with suspected mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections. From an initial 24 suspected cases, we confirmed 17 as genuine coinfections and graded them by evidence
papers.summary: This study tracked 24 military cohort participants with suspected mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections, confirming 17 as genuine coinfections and grading the strength of evidence for each. By characterizing viral populations over time, the authors found that distinct viral genotypes can occupy different anatomical compartments within the same host, suggesting compartmentalized viral dynamics that could influence recombination and variant emergence.

papers.title: Scalable assembly of Ascaris mitogenomes from whole-genome data reveals a novel clade.
papers.abstract: The genus Ascaris is an important group of giant parasitic roundworms, infecting over 700 million people globally and causing substantial economic losses in domestic pigs. Whilst species of Ascaris are morphologically indistinguishable, analysis of mitochondrial loci has revealed three clades (A, B, C) broadly associated with host species and geographic distribution. The diversity within these lineages may expand with the addition of further genomic data. Here, we present a bioinformatic framework for de novo assembly of complete mitochondrial genomes (mitogenomes) from low-coverage whole-geno
papers.summary: The authors developed a bioinformatic pipeline to assemble complete Ascaris mitochondrial genomes from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data. Applying it to existing datasets, they uncovered a novel mitochondrial clade, expanding the known diversity of this globally important parasite genus. The approach enables scalable mitogenome recovery without dedicated mitochondrial enrichment.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other a
papers.summary: The authors developed Epi2Hit, a computational method that integrates whole-genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling, and gene expression data to detect biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes via a 'second hit' mechanism: epigenetic silencing (promoter/enhancer methylation) of one allele combined with genomic loss of the other. Applying this to prostate cancer, they identified new putative tumour suppressor genes that would be missed by conventional approaches focused on homozygous deletion.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1- patient variant R5179, corresp
papers.summary: This study generated a mouse model of Kabuki syndrome type 1 carrying a patient-derived missense variant (R5179) in the KMT2D histone methyltransferase using CRISPR-Cas9. The work addresses the gap that most existing KS1 mouse models use loss-of-function alleles, while 15-30% of patients carry missense variants. It enables investigation of whether missense variants produce comparable phenotypes and may inform therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling Primer: Focus on Chromatin and Epigenetics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in modern biology is to understand how molecular interactions produce cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales. Nowhere is this challenge more apparent than in the study of chromatin, where meters of DNA compact into a micron-sized nucleus. How this polymer folds is a dynamic process, regulated by epigenetic modifications-chemical changes to DNA and histones that involve only a handful of atoms. These small changes cooperate to produce emergent, higher-order structures that define cellular identity and function. To explain this system, we must int
papers.summary: This primer explains how multiscale modeling can bridge the gap between atomic-level epigenetic modifications and the large-scale folding of chromatin within the nucleus. It argues that understanding how tiny chemical changes to DNA and histones produce emergent higher-order chromatin structures requires integrating models across vastly different spatial and temporal scales. The paper serves as an accessible introduction to the concepts and methods needed to study chromatin and epigenetics through a multiscale lens.

papers.title: GenoME: a MoE-based generative model for individualized, multimodal prediction and perturbation of genomic profiles.
papers.abstract: The non-coding genome operates through a complex, multiscale regulatory system where regulated gene expressions are closely associated with cell-type-specific histone modifications, transcription factor binding, and 3D conformation. Developing computational models that can integrate these patterns to predict and interpret the regulatory system remains challenging. Here, we present GenoME, a Mixture of Experts (MoE)-based generative model that uses DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict a unified genomic profiles encompassing epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin
papers.summary: GenoME is a Mixture-of-Experts generative model that takes DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq data as input to predict multimodal genomic profiles, including epigenomic, transcriptomic, and chromatin features. It aims to capture the multiscale regulatory system of the non-coding genome and enable individualized prediction and perturbation of these profiles.

papers.title: DNA methylation-based ageing in a deuterostome invertebrate: an epigenetic clock for the crown-of-thorns seastar (Acanthaster cf. solaris).
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable ageing tools are essential for wildlife conservation and management. While DNA methylation has emerged as a promising tool for age estimation in vertebrates, its application to invertebrates remains contested and has been limited to arthropods. Here, we develop an epigenetic clock for the Pacific crown-of-thorns seastar (CoTS; Acanthaster cf. solaris), a destructive coral predator contributing to habitat degradation across Indo-Pacific reefs. Using Oxford Nanopore Technologies, we generated whole-genome DNA methylation profiles across five age groups and identified 1910 C
papers.summary: This study developed the first DNA methylation-based epigenetic clock for an echinoderm, the crown-of-thorns seastar, using Oxford Nanopore whole-genome methylation profiling across five age groups. They identified 1,910 age-associated CpG sites, extending epigenetic ageing tools beyond vertebrates and arthropods to a deuterostome invertebrate of major ecological concern.

papers.title: Co-Directional Chromosomal Clustering of Metabolic Pathway Genes as a Layout Prior for Synthetic Construct Design.
papers.abstract: Metabolic pathway design tools largely address reaction routes and enzyme choice, whereas a complementary set of questions-how pathway genes are arranged on bacterial chromosomes and whether co-directional neighborhoods can inform multi-gene construct layout-has received comparatively little systematic treatment. Here, we present SynPAL (Synteny-Informed Pathway Assembly and Layout), a computational analysis that scores co-directional clustering of BioCyc pathway genes from genomic coordinates (same replicon and strand, intergenic distance ≤ 2000 bp) and translates the resulting scores into de
papers.summary: The authors present SynPAL, a computational tool that scores how frequently genes of BioCyc metabolic pathways are clustered co-directionally on bacterial chromosomes (same strand, within 2000 bp). These synteny-derived scores are then used as a layout prior to guide the arrangement of multi-gene synthetic constructs, connecting natural genomic organization to pathway engineering design.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models, focusing on two classes: genomic sequence models that treat nucleotides as tokens and cell foundation models that learn transferable representations of cellular states. It argues these models can integrate genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular context to better understand and translate findings for complex diseases like cancer and neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequence Dataset of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267-Terpenoid Biotransformer Toward Genetic Functional Annotation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Microbial biotransformation of monoterpenoids is a promising approach for obtaining bioactive compounds. Rhodococcus species are attractive biocatalysts due to their metabolic versatility and ability to transform hydrophobic substrates. In this study, we investigated the catalytic potential of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267 toward carveol isomers and explored genomic features that may underlie this activity. Methods: The strain was cultivated in mineral medium supplemented with (-)-trans-carveol. Biotransformation products were analyzed by TLC and GC-MS. The draft geno
papers.summary: This study reports the draft whole-genome sequence of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267, a bacterium capable of biotransforming monoterpenoids such as carveol isomers. The genome was analyzed alongside GC-MS and TLC characterization of biotransformation products to identify genetic features potentially responsible for this catalytic activity. The dataset provides a foundation for functional annotation of terpenoid-transforming enzymes in Rhodococcus.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Listeria monocytogenes Isolated from Retail Yak Meat in Nyingchi, Xizang, China.
papers.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a Gram-positive zoonotic pathogen responsible for listeriosis, a severe foodborne disease with high mortality in humans and animals. This study aimed to investigate the molecular epidemiology and genomic characteristics of L. monocytogenes isolated from raw yak meat in Nyingchi, Xizang, China. A total of 231 yak-related samples were collected in Nyingchi, consisting of 214 retail raw yak meat samples, 14 farm environmental samples, and 3 nearby water source samples. L. monocytogenes isolates were identified and characterized using culture-based methods, PCR serotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study surveyed Listeria monocytogenes contamination in raw yak meat and related environmental samples from Nyingchi, Xizang, China, identifying and characterizing isolates through culture-based methods and PCR serotyping. It provides baseline molecular epidemiological and genomic data on this foodborne pathogen in a region where such surveillance is limited.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stereo-Seq Spatial Transcriptomic Resource for Adult Holstein Cattle Liver.
papers.abstract: The bovine liver is a highly compartmentalized organ that plays essential roles in continuous gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling; however, its spatial molecular architecture has remained largely uncharacterized due to the limitations of traditional bulk and single-cell approaches. To address this gap, Spatial Enhanced Resolution Omics-sequencing (Stereo-seq) was utilized to generate a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver, and a refined reference-guided workflow was implemented to overcome standard annotation limitations in livestock. Raw sequ
papers.summary: This study generated a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) spatial transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver using Stereo-seq, providing the first detailed spatial molecular atlas of the bovine liver. The authors also developed a refined reference-guided workflow to improve gene annotation in livestock species where standard annotations are incomplete. The resource reveals the spatial organization of hepatic compartments and their roles in gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling.

papers.title: Whole mitogenome profile of Pelung and Sentul chickens to reveal potency of Indonesian livestock genetic resources.
papers.abstract: Native chickens are essential genetic resources in Indonesia, providing economic, cultural, and nutritional value with strong adaptability to local environments. Among these native chickens, Sentul and Pelung are recognized as national genetic resources due to dual-purpose and ornamental traits, respectively, but their whole mitogenome characterization remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to assemble and analyze the whole mitogenome of Sentul and Pelung chickens as well as perform a comparison with 35 additional genomes from domestic chickens and jungle fowls across Asia. The experimen
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the complete mitochondrial genomes of two Indonesian native chicken breeds, Sentul and Pelung, and compared them with 35 additional mitogenomes from domestic chickens and jungle fowls across Asia. The findings characterize the genetic diversity and phylogenetic relationships of these national genetic resources, providing baseline genomic data to support their conservation and breeding programs.

papers.title: The bioinformatics approach to identifying pathogenic variants for colorectal cancer (CRC).
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most prevalent cancer globally, accounting for 9.6% of newly diagnosed cases and 9.3% of cancer-related deaths. It develops from the uncontrolled proliferation of glandular cells in the colon and rectum and is categorized into three primary types: sporadic, hereditary, and colitis-associated. While genetic susceptibility is a key factor in CRC pathogenesis, identifying high-impact pathogenic variants remains a significant challenge. This study integrates bioinformatics and population genetics approaches to identify CRC-associated single-nucleotide polymorph
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics and population genetics methods to identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms and other pathogenic variants associated with colorectal cancer. It aims to address the challenge of pinpointing high-impact genetic variants that contribute to CRC susceptibility across sporadic, hereditary, and colitis-associated forms.

papers.title: Unlocking cis-regulatory landscapes across 500 million years of evolution and disease mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Genomic DNA encodes regulatory information that determines where, when, and to what extent genes are expressed. Theoretically, we should be able to identify these transcriptional "instructions" by examining genomic DNA sequence alone, yet this has remained challenging. Here we present the Vertebrate Regulatory MOdule Detector (VRMOD), a method that accurately predicts gene regulatory sequences using only the query genomic sequences. We applied VRMOD to 309 Ensembl genomes, generating a compendium of high-resolution, genome-position-fixed cis-regulatory modules without parameter tuning. We perf
papers.summary: The authors present VRMOD, a method that predicts cis-regulatory modules directly from genomic sequence without requiring parameter tuning or species-specific training data. They applied it across 309 Ensembl vertebrate genomes, producing a cross-species compendium of high-resolution regulatory elements spanning 500 million years of evolution. This resource enables comparative regulatory genomics and helps link non-coding disease variants to gene regulation.

papers.title: JanusX: an integrated and high-performance platform for scalable genome-wide association studies and genomic selection.
papers.abstract: As genomic datasets expand in both sample size and marker density, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and genomic selection (GS) require workflows that remain statistically rigorous, computationally efficient, and reproducible across the full analysis path, from genotype matrix to decision-relevant outputs. Here we present JanusX, an integrated high-performance framework that provides a streamlined, user-oriented workflow for GWAS and GS by unifying data handling, model execution, and visualization. Across simulated and real datasets, JanusX maintained high concordance with established bas
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: JanusX is an integrated high-performance platform that unifies data handling, model execution, and visualization for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and genomic selection (GS). It maintains high concordance with established methods across simulated and real datasets while offering a streamlined, reproducible workflow from genotype matrix to decision-relevant outputs.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and emerging approaches—highlighting the strengths and limitations of each. The review is aimed at experienced practitioners and developers seeking a structured overview of the rapidly expanding phage bioinformatics landscape.

papers.title: Nanopore metagenomic sequencing links clinically relevant resistance determinants to pathogens.
papers.abstract: Culture-independent metagenomics enables the detection of plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes directly from clinical samples; however, the clinical significance of these genes depends on their bacterial host and genomic context, which metagenomics cannot fully infer. Nanopore sequencing technology intrinsically encodes epigenetic modifications such as methylation, which can be leveraged for plasmid-host associations from metagenomic data. Existing methods rely on the recovery of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), which can introduce bias towards abundant taxa and leave clini
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomic sequencing, which captures DNA methylation signals, to link plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance genes directly to their bacterial hosts in clinical samples without culturing. This overcomes the limitation of standard metagenomics, which detects resistance genes but cannot determine which pathogen carries them, and avoids the abundance bias of metagenome-assembled genome approaches.

papers.title: metaKEGG: A comprehensive algorithm package to visualize multi-omics pathway enrichment.
papers.abstract: metaKEGG is a comprehensive software package designed to streamline the visualization and integration of pathway enrichment results from multi-omics data, providing accessible and detailed insights into the molecular mechanisms driving health and disease. Unlike standard pipeline approaches, metaKEGG incorporates novel concepts allowing for clear, granular representation of gene-level or transcript-level expression changes. Beyond transcriptomic analysis, metaKEGG also supports epigenetic and regulatory metadata layers, such as methylation profiles and miRNA target annotations, offering users
papers.summary: metaKEGG is a software package that visualizes and integrates pathway enrichment results across multiple omics layers, including transcriptomic, epigenetic, and regulatory data such as methylation and miRNA targets. It introduces novel concepts for granular gene- or transcript-level representation of expression changes, going beyond standard pathway enrichment pipelines.

papers.title: Establishment of a Common Marmoset Lineage Carrying a Frameshift Mutation in SETD1A, a Schizophrenia Risk Gene.
papers.abstract: Appropriate histone modifications are essential for maintaining functional chromatin structure and gene expression, and dysfunction of their regulators has been linked to a variety of diseases. Among these modifications, trimethylation of lysine 4 on histone H3 (H3K4me3) is a well-characterized epigenetic mark enriched at transcription start sites of actively transcribed genes. H3K4me3 regulates gene transcription by recruiting transcription factors, facilitating chromatin accessibility, and preventing DNA methylation. In mammals, methylation of H3K4 is catalyzed by a family of histone methylt
papers.summary: This study establishes a common marmoset lineage carrying a frameshift mutation in SETD1A, a gene encoding an H3K4me3 histone methyltransferase that is a known schizophrenia risk gene. The marmoset model is intended to enable investigation of how loss of SETD1A function affects brain development and behavior in a primate context, which may better recapitulate human disease features than rodent models.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer diagnosis. It addresses limitations of prior methods that treat sequence and methylation features separately and struggle with low-signal liquid biopsy data.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework for automatically annotating cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data, addressing the lack of specialized tools for this data type. It leverages multi-scale information to handle the distinct distribution of scDNAm data and provides interpretable results.

papers.title: Sotagliflozin, a Dual SGLT1/2 Inhibitor, Modulates DNMT1 and Class I/II HDAC Expression in Association With Anticancer Effects in Breast and Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors are increasingly recognised for anticancer activity beyond their established glycaemic effects. While selective SGLT2 inhibitors have been reported to suppress tumour cell proliferation and modulate AMPK/mTOR and PI3K/AKT signalling, whether dual SGLT1/2 inhibition is associated with modulation of epigenetic regulators has remained largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the anticancer effects of sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. Sotagliflozin reduced cell viability, clonogenic survival, mig
papers.summary: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, reduced viability, clonogenic survival, and migration in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. The anticancer effects were accompanied by changes in expression of the epigenetic regulators DNMT1 and class I/II HDACs, suggesting a link between SGLT inhibition and epigenetic modulation.

papers.title: Natural compounds as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers: From chemoresistance to precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Gynaecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial malignancies, remain major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality because of tumour heterogeneity, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. Epigenetic dysregulation, involving aberrant DNA methylation, altered histone modifications, dysregulated non-coding RNAs, and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) RNA remodelling, contributes to these processes. Direct evidence that natural compounds modulate m⁶A machinery in gynaecological cancers remains absent and is considered a knowledge gap.
papers.summary: This review examines how natural compounds can act as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers (ovarian, cervical, endometrial), focusing on DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, and m6A RNA modification as drivers of chemoresistance. The authors highlight that direct evidence for natural compounds targeting m6A machinery in these cancers is currently lacking, identifying this as a key knowledge gap for future precision oncology research.

papers.title: Comprehensive epigenetic landscape of Sulfur Mustard (SM) exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.abstract: Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a potent vesicant chemical agent with profound and complex toxic effects. Traditionally, its toxic mechanism has been attributed to DNA alkylation-induced cytotoxicity and genomic instability. However, growing evidence indicates that dysregulation of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms constitutes a central link in SM toxicity, particularly in its long-term and delayed effects. Our study establishes an in vitro SM exposure model and employs integrated multi-omics profiling-including six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and non-coding RNA analyses-to s
papers.summary: This study builds an in vitro model of sulfur mustard exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes and profiles six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomes, and non-coding RNAs to map the epigenetic response. The integrated multi-omics view suggests epigenetic dysregulation is a central mechanism underlying SM toxicity and its delayed effects, beyond classical DNA alkylation damage.

papers.title: DiffMethylTools: a toolbox for the detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic mechanism, and its significant changes (i.e., differential methylation) regulate gene expression, cell-type specification, and disease progression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Differential methylation has traditionally been detected by statistical comparison of two groups using existing tools and has supported a wide range of downstream analyses in human disease studies. However, few toolboxes efficiently integrate robust detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation, and the reproducibility of detected signals
papers.summary: DiffMethylTools is a new software toolbox that integrates detection, annotation, and visualization of differential DNA methylation from bisulfite sequencing data. It aims to streamline the analysis pipeline and improve reproducibility compared to using separate tools for each step. The toolbox is designed for researchers studying epigenetic changes in diseases and cell-type specification.

papers.title: ECHO: a nanopore sequencing-based workflow for (epi)genetic profiling of the human repeatome.
papers.abstract: The human genome is dominated by repetitive DNA, whose genetic and epigenetic variation plays a key role in gene regulation, genome stability, and disease. Recent advances in long-read sequencing now enable large-scale, haplotype-resolved, and DNA methylation-informative analysis of the human genome, including on previously inaccessible complex and repetitive regions. However, the comprehensive, simultaneous characterisation of the "human repeatome" remains challenging, largely due to the lack of comprehensive tools integrated in a single pipeline that can capture the full spectrum of variatio
papers.summary: ECHO is a new nanopore sequencing-based workflow that simultaneously profiles genetic and epigenetic (methylation) variation across the human repeatome, the large fraction of the genome made up of repetitive DNA. It addresses the lack of integrated tools capable of capturing the full spectrum of repeat variation in a single pipeline, enabling haplotype-resolved analysis of these previously inaccessible regions.

papers.title: nf-core/pacsomatic: a scalable somatic analytic pipeline using PacBio HiFi data.
papers.abstract: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) HiFi long-read sequencing enables robust characterization of complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants (SVs) that are often inaccessible to short-read technologies. To fully leverage HiFi reads to advance cancer genomics and epigenetics, researchers require an end-to-end, scalable and optimized bioinformatics workflow. The nf-core framework meets this need by providing rigorously tested, community-curated pipelines that ensure reproducibility, transparency, and broad compatibility across computational environments.
papers.summary: The authors present nf-core/pacsomatic, a scalable end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline for somatic variant and epigenetic analysis using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing data. Built within the nf-core framework, it offers reproducible, community-curated workflows that handle complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants often missed by short-read approaches. The pipeline aims to make HiFi-based cancer genomics accessible across diverse computational environments.

papers.title: Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox: An Integrative Framework for Endpoint-Conditioned Evidentiary Sufficiency in Structure-to-Function Claims.
papers.abstract: Accurate coordinates for a represented protein state do not, by themselves, establish activity or any other condition-specific function. This article defines the Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox (DPSP) as the apparent conflict between structural accuracy and functional underdetermination and develops it as an integrative evidentiary assessment framework rather than a new theory or paradigm. The underlying problem has been longstanding, since structural genomics, function annotation, allostery, and disorder research each established that fold does not determine function and that function does
papers.summary: This article formalizes the 'Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox'—the observation that accurate protein coordinates alone cannot establish function—and proposes an integrative framework for assessing when structural evidence is sufficient to support structure-to-function claims. Rather than presenting a new theory, it synthesizes longstanding insights from structural genomics, allostery, and disorder research into a practical evidentiary assessment approach.

papers.title: Beyond Canonical Neoantigens: Emerging Technologies for Identification of Noncanonical Antigens and Implications for Personalized Cancer Vaccines.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, advances in sequencing technologies and computational pipelines enabled the development of personalized cancer vaccines (PCVs). Current PCV strategies primarily target cancer neoantigens generated by non-synonymous DNA mutations, which can result in altered amino acid sequences capable of eliciting tumor-specific immune responses. More recently, a distinct class of tumor-specific antigens (TSA), termed noncanonical or cryptic antigens, has emerged as an additional source of immunogenic targets. Unlike canonical neoantigens, noncanonical antigens typically cannot be identi
papers.summary: This review discusses how personalized cancer vaccines have traditionally targeted neoantigens arising from DNA mutations, but a new class of tumor-specific antigens called noncanonical or cryptic antigens is emerging as an additional source of immunogenic targets. The authors survey emerging technologies for identifying these noncanonical antigens and consider their implications for improving personalized cancer vaccine design.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review compares deep learning architectures—convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph neural networks—for modeling plant cis-regulatory information from DNA sequence and multi-omics data. It assesses their use in predicting transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and prioritizing non-coding variants relevant to agronomic traits.

papers.title: Pangenomes aid accurate detection of large insertions and deletions from targeted sequencing: the case of cardiomyopathies.
papers.abstract: Gene panels represent a widely used strategy for genetic testing in a vast range of Mendelian disorders. While this approach aids reliable bioinformatic detection of short coding variants, it often fails to detect many larger variants. Recent studies have recommended the adoption of pangenome references (as opposed to linear reference genomes like GRCh38) to augment detection of large variants from targeted sequencing, potentially providing diagnostic laboratories with the possibility to streamline diagnostic work-ups and reduce costs.
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether pangenome references improve the detection of large insertions and deletions (indels) from targeted gene panel sequencing, using cardiomyopathies as a test case. The authors show that pangenome-based analysis can identify clinically relevant large variants that are missed when using the standard linear reference genome GRCh38. This suggests diagnostic laboratories could adopt pangenome references to streamline testing and reduce costs.

papers.title: Integrative Molecular Profiling of miR-548f-3p in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Highlights ANP32E as a Candidate Downstream Effector.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a major therapeutic challenge due to pronounced molecular heterogeneity, transcriptional plasticity, and frequent treatment resistance. MicroRNA (miRNA)-based strategies have emerged as potential approaches for modulating dysregulated gene expression networks in TNBC; however, the contribution of understudied miRNA families to TNBC-associated regulatory programs remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the tumor-suppressive role of miR-548f-3p in TNBC and to identify candidate downstream effectors, with particular focus on AN
papers.summary: This study investigates the tumor-suppressive role of the understudied microRNA miR-548f-3p in triple-negative breast cancer and identifies ANP32E as a candidate downstream effector through integrative molecular profiling. The findings suggest that miR-548f-3p may modulate dysregulated gene expression networks in TNBC, offering a potential molecular target for this hard-to-treat cancer subtype.

papers.title: Residual based anomaly detection framework for variant caller dispatch in DNA sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Reliable and scalable variant analysis is an enabling component of genomic studies involving microbial communities, host-associated microorganisms, and their hosts, and may support future investigations of genetic heterogeneity within symbiotic systems. Widely used workflows incorporating BWA and GATK provide standardized default processing routes, but their performance may vary across genomic regions containing repetitive sequences, complex structures, or atypical local sequence characteristics. Applying a context-aware software-recommendation procedure to every genomic region, however, can s
papers.summary: The paper introduces a residual-based anomaly detection framework that decides which variant caller to use for different genomic regions in DNA sequencing data. By flagging regions with unusual sequence characteristics, it enables context-aware dispatch of variant-calling tools instead of relying on a single default workflow. This aims to improve reliability of variant analysis, particularly for microbial and host-associated genomic studies.

papers.title: Alzheimer's disease: genetic background in the era of next-generation sequencing technologies.
papers.abstract: While rare, highly penetrant variants in APP, PSEN1 and PSEN2 are associated with early-onset Alzheimer's disease, especially its familial form, the disease in general is shaped by a complex interplay of various genetic factors. Both common and rare variants across numerous loci, which were identified mainly during large genome-wide association studies, contribute to disease risk, phenotypic heterogeneity and progression in both early- and late-onset forms. This review synthesizes current understanding of the genetic architecture of Alzheimer's disease in the era of next-generation sequencing,
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge of Alzheimer's disease genetics, covering rare high-penetrance variants in APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 that cause early-onset familial forms, as well as common and rare risk variants across many loci identified through genome-wide association studies. It emphasizes how next-generation sequencing has revealed the complex polygenic architecture underlying disease risk, heterogeneity, and progression in both early- and late-onset Alzheimer's.

papers.title: Potential Contribution of DES (p.Leu88Met) and MYH7 (p.Arg787His) Variants to Familial Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) is a rare, severe cardiac disease with a heterogeneous genetic basis. Both genetic and nongenetic factors contribute to RCM pathogenesis. Identifying the underlying molecular causes is important for diagnosis and family screening. In this study, we investigated the genetic basis of RCM in a 52-year-old woman with a family history of RCM and heart disease.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 52-year-old woman with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) who carries two rare genetic variants: DES p.Leu88Met and MYH7 p.Arg787His. The authors propose that these variants may contribute to the disease, highlighting the potential oligogenic nature of RCM and the value of genetic testing for diagnosis and family screening.

papers.title: REAPER: a project-centric workflow layer for comparative repeatome analysis.
papers.abstract: Repeatome characterization from short-read sequencing data is widely performed using RepeatExplorer2/TAREAN. However, long-lived multisample projects and explicit comparative designs are often executed as ad hoc command sequences that are hard to version, rerun, and monitor on shared compute environments - a gap that motivates a project-centric workflow layer for repeatome analysis.
papers.summary: REAPER is a workflow layer built on top of RepeatExplorer2/TAREAN that organizes repeatome analysis around long-lived, multi-sample comparative projects rather than ad hoc command sequences. It aims to make repeat annotation workflows easier to version, rerun, and monitor on shared compute environments.

papers.title: Short-read genome skimming enables molecular barcoding of old myxomycete collections.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Illumina-based genome skimming for barcoding myxomycete herbarium collections ranging from 29 to 91 years in age. We successfully retrieved partial sequences of the standard marker gene (nucSSU) in all cases, as well as additional markers (mtSSU, EF1a, and COI) for certain collections. Altogether, 28 genes were recognized in the studied material. In a 33-year-old specimen of Lindbladia tubulina, the assembly reached an N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling the recovery of extended functional loci. The input genomic DNA quantity emerges as the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study shows that Illumina genome skimming can successfully recover barcode sequences from myxomycete herbarium specimens up to 91 years old, retrieving the standard nucSSU marker in all samples and additional markers in some. The amount of input genomic DNA was the main factor determining success, and one 33-year-old specimen yielded an assembly with N50 of 4.19 kb, allowing recovery of extended functional loci.

papers.title: 'PePApipe': A complete bioinformatics analysis pipeline for African Swine Fever Virus genome.
papers.abstract: African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) is of high concern in porcine livestock across the world due to both the high mortality rates and the trade restrictions imposed on affected regions. The viral genome is large and complex, and genomic analysis is essential for tracing its origin and evolution. Although several bioinformatics tools exist for genome assembly and analysis, no single platform integrates all necessary steps in an accessible and systematic way. In this study the authors developed 'PePApipe', a custom-built, user-friendly pipeline that enables rapid, complete, and efficient ASFV genom
papers.summary: The authors developed 'PePApipe', a user-friendly bioinformatics pipeline that integrates all steps needed for African Swine Fever Virus genome assembly and analysis into a single platform. This addresses the lack of a unified tool for ASFV genomics, which is important for tracking the virus's origin and evolution during outbreaks.

papers.title: Correlation assessment of SARS-CoV-2 variants and their subvariants present in clinical and wastewater samples in Oregon, USA (February 7, 2021 - February 26, 2022) using the Freyja bioinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance is a valuable tool for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 at the community level. As the virus diversified into many variants and subvariants that share overlapping mutations, resolving them accurately from wastewater becomes a key bioinformatic challenge.
papers.summary: This study applied the Freyja bioinformatics tool to compare SARS-CoV-2 variant and subvariant composition in clinical samples versus wastewater samples collected across Oregon over roughly a year. The authors assessed how well wastewater-based sequencing reflects the variants circulating in the community, addressing the challenge of distinguishing variants that share overlapping mutations.

papers.title: In silico transcriptomic analysis nominates TSPAN32 as a central node of SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming in intestinal epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: Microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) regulate intestinal epithelial homeostasis and immune tolerance. Yet, the specific host effector genes that mediate these responses remain poorly defined, limiting the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) analysis of transcriptomic data to identify host genes that respond to microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in intestinal epithelial cells. The analysis nominates TSPAN32 as a central hub gene in SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming, suggesting it may serve as a biomarker or therapeutic target. The findings are computational predictions that would require experimental validation.

papers.title: From sequence to timescale: a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework linking ncRNA sequence composition to epigenetic regulatory timescales.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are central regulators of epigenomic states, orchestrating chromatin modifications, gene silencing, and nuclear architecture through recruitment of chromatin-modifying complexes. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) such as XIST, HOTAIR, and MALAT1 exemplify these regulatory roles. Despite their importance, quantitative computational frameworks for linking ncRNA sequence composition to temporal regulatory behaviour remain limited. We introduce a frequency-domain control theory framework modelling RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, extending a previously established s
papers.summary: The authors propose a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework that models non-coding RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, aiming to link sequence composition to the timescales of epigenetic regulation. This extends prior work by providing a quantitative computational approach to connect ncRNA sequence features with temporal regulatory dynamics, using examples like XIST, HOTAIR, and MALAT1.

papers.title: The metastatic spectrum in functional and non-functional NENs: mechanistic insights from multi-omics.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are biologically heterogeneous tumors in which differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but non-equivalent axes. This review focuses on functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), principally gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic NETs, and critically evaluates how site, lineage, stage, tumor burden, genomic and epigenetic alterations, immune-stromal remodeling, metabolic adaptation, microbiome-associated signals, and treatment pressure converge on metastasis and recurrence. Apparent outcome differences
papers.summary: This review examines how functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), mainly gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic, differ in their metastatic behavior. It integrates multi-omics evidence—genomic, epigenetic, immune-stromal, metabolic, and microbiome signals—to argue that differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but distinct axes shaping metastasis and recurrence. The authors critically evaluate how tumor site, lineage, stage, and treatment pressure converge on metastatic outcomes.
